daily.brief: 過去約26小時（11月26日晚上7:30至27日晚上9:29）134個帳號發了407則帖，多頭觀點110個、空頭26個。共同看好集中在$AMZN、$META、$MSFT這類大型科技股；沒有純共同看淡標的。最熱鬧的$NVDA有62則提及，多空帳號9對5。
daily.full:
共識

共同看好以大型科技為主。$AMZN有2個帳號同向：@BrianFeroldi問亞馬遜在$250是買入嗎？偉大的業務，公允估值（原帖）；@damnang2轉推昨天DELL今天MSFT「AI才剛開始」，我們只是剛開始AI革命，提到$MU $NBIS $AMZN $AVGO（原帖）。$META同樣2個，@InvestmentGuru_指出在沒有新聞的情況下錄得當天最佳大市值反轉，開盤575.34美元，低點567.75美元，收盤609.89美元上漲3.4%，接近高點611.06美元，從低點回升7.4%，盤後守住611.43美元（原帖）；@wliang覺得最安全的股票會是像$GOOGL、$META、$NVDA、$SPCX這樣（原帖）。$MSFT有2個，@MikeZaccardi說MSFT是唯一沒有將自由現金流轉負的超大規模雲服務商（原帖）。

共同看淡

這段期間沒有純共同看淡的標的出現在列表上。空頭觀點整體較少，只有26個，主要散落在分歧標的裡。

分歧

分歧最大的是$NVDA，62則提及中多空帳號9對5。@danielnewmanUV澄清到2030年華為「可能有」相當於目前NVIDIA的東西，但絕無可能達到同等水平，對人們相信Qwen、DeepSeek等在沒有領先AI晶片的情況下能如此快速進步感到驚訝（原帖）；@DrJStrategy說空頭說2027或2028年沒有AI需求是錯的，高盛預測DRAM在2027年短缺5.1%，是15年多來最寬的缺口（原帖）；@unusual_whales轉NYT報導華為晶片今年預計只提供Nvidia AI計算能力的不到4%，且不太可能在2030年左右匹配目前產出（原帖）。$SPCX多空9對1，@BillAckman談複利的力量，引用女兒今年從Elon獲得兩股SpaceX，每年再加一股的例子（原帖）。$TSLA多空8對2，@firesidealpha說德州DMV今日一小時內註冊了285輛更多Cybercab，是迄今最大批次，車隊現有1841輛（原帖）。

其他值得留意

$RKLB有2個帳號看好，@StockSavvyShay與@SpaceInvestor_D都提到成功完成第101次Electron發射。$GOOGL與$DELL也各有2個共同看好，討論集中在AI數據中心與生產力提升。

weekly.brief: 過去7日（11月21日至27日）299個帳號發了2669則帖。共同看好最多的是$CRWD（7個帳號）與$RKLB（5個）；共同看淡則是$ORCL（7個）與$AMBA（5個）。$NVDA一週提及678次，多空帳號41對32。
weekly.full:
共識

一週內共同看好以網絡安全與部分成長名稱為主。$CRWD有7個帳號同向，@StockMarketNerd指出CRWD仍然是精英業務，估值反映這一點，在一片漂亮季度中又一個漂亮季度，出色指引尤其是淨新增ARR上調（原帖）；@TradexWhisperer提到OpenRouter的token量一年內上升35倍，代理工作負載現約佔80%（原帖）。$RKLB有5個，@StockSavvyShay與@SpaceInvestor_D都提到成功完成第101次Electron發射。$ADSK、$LLY各有4個。

共同看淡

$ORCL有7個帳號看淡。@CheddarFlow說Oracle的信用違約掉期合約現在比Bear Stearns在2008年1月時更寬，債券市場正在像2007年那樣為AI建設定價（原帖）；@carlquintanilla轉推指出管理層根本誤解了投資者為何擔心其AI資本支出狂潮，不是執行風險，而是交易對手和集中度風險（原帖）。$AMBA有5個，@carlquintanilla轉推CEO說記憶體價格前所未有的上漲及供應稀缺已加劇，導致許多客戶降低展望，盤後-37%（原帖）。

分歧

$NVDA一週678次提及，多空帳號41對32。SPCX 25對7偏向多頭，SPY 20對9，ANT 11對17偏向空頭。整體討論量擴大，高提及標的的多空分歧持續存在。

其他值得留意

網絡安全名稱如CRWD維持較一致正面討論，ORCL的信貸擔憂在一週內明顯累積，AMBA則受記憶體價格衝擊。

daily.brief: Over roughly the last 26 hours (7:30pm on Nov 26 to 9:29pm on Nov 27), 134 accounts posted 407 times, with 110 bullish views and 26 bearish ones. Shared bullish views concentrated on large tech names like $AMZN, $META and $MSFT; there were no pure shared bearish names. The busiest name $NVDA had 62 mentions with 9 bullish versus 5 bearish accounts.
daily.full:
Consensus

Shared bullish views centered on large tech. $AMZN had 2 accounts aligned: @BrianFeroldi asked if Amazon at $250 is a buy, calling it a great business at fair valuation (post); @damnang2 reposted that yesterday DELL today MSFT "AI has just begun", we are only at the start of the AI revolution, mentioning $MU $NBIS $AMZN $AVGO (post). $META also had 2; @InvestmentGuru_ pointed to the best large-cap reversal of the day with no news, open $575.34, low $567.75, close $609.89 up 3.4% near the high of $611.06, up 7.4% from the low, holding $611.43 after hours (post); @wliang said the safest stocks would be like $GOOGL, $META, $NVDA, $SPCX (post). $MSFT had 2; @MikeZaccardi said MSFT is the only hyperscaler that has not turned free cash flow negative (post).

Shared Bearish

There were no pure shared bearish names on the list for this period. Bearish views were fewer overall at only 26, mostly scattered in the split names.

Split

The largest split was on $NVDA, with 9 bullish versus 5 bearish accounts among 62 mentions. @danielnewmanUV clarified that by 2030 Huawei "may have" something equivalent to current NVIDIA but will absolutely not reach the same level, surprised that people believe Qwen, DeepSeek etc. can progress so fast without leading AI chips (post); @DrJStrategy said the bears claiming no AI demand in 2027 or 2028 are wrong, Goldman Sachs forecasts DRAM shortage of 5.1% in 2027, the widest gap in over 15 years (post); @unusual_whales cited NYT that Huawei chips are expected to provide less than 4% of Nvidia AI compute capacity this year and are unlikely to match current output around 2030 (post). $SPCX was 9 versus 1; @BillAckman talked about the power of compounding, citing his daughter receiving two SpaceX shares from Elon this year plus one each year (post). $TSLA was 8 versus 2; @firesidealpha said Texas DMV registered 285 more Cybercabs in one hour today, the largest batch yet, with the fleet now at 1,841 (post).

Other Notable

$RKLB had 2 bullish accounts; @StockSavvyShay and @SpaceInvestor_D both noted the successful 101st Electron launch. $GOOGL and $DELL also each had 2 shared bullish views, with discussion around AI data centers and productivity gains.

weekly.brief: Over the past 7 days (Nov 21 to 27), 299 accounts posted 2669 times. Shared bullish views concentrated on $CRWD (7 accounts) and $RKLB (5); shared bearish on $ORCL (7) and $AMBA (5). $NVDA had 678 mentions for the week with 41 bullish versus 32 bearish accounts.
weekly.full:
Consensus

Shared bullish views over the week centered on cybersecurity and selected growth names. $CRWD had 7 accounts aligned; @StockMarketNerd noted CRWD remains an elite business with valuation reflecting that, another beautiful quarter in a string of them, outstanding guidance especially the raised net new ARR (post); @TradexWhisperer mentioned OpenRouter token volume up 35x in a year, with agent workloads now about 80% (post). $RKLB had 5; @StockSavvyShay and @SpaceInvestor_D both noted the successful 101st Electron launch. $ADSK and $LLY each had 4.

Shared Bearish

$ORCL had 7 bearish accounts. @CheddarFlow said Oracle's credit default swaps are now wider than Bear Stearns in January 2008, with the bond market pricing AI builds like 2007 (post); @carlquintanilla shared that management fundamentally misunderstood why investors worry about the AI capex frenzy, not execution risk but counterparty and concentration risk (post). $AMBA had 5; @carlquintanilla shared the CEO saying unprecedented memory price rises and supply scarcity have intensified, leading many customers to lower outlooks, down 37% after hours (post).

Split

$NVDA had 678 mentions for the week with 41 bullish versus 32 bearish accounts. SPCX 25 versus 7 tilted bullish, SPY 20 versus 9, ANT 11 versus 17 tilted bearish. Overall discussion volume expanded and splits on high-mention names continued.

Other Notable

Cybersecurity names like CRWD maintained relatively consistent positive discussion, ORCL's credit concerns accumulated over the week, and AMBA was hit by memory prices.
